To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
spinal nerve lesion in rats results in an upregu-lation of HO-2 and CO which is somehow contribut-ing to the neurodegeneration in the spinal cord.
spinal nerve injury induces an upregulation in the expression of the constitutively active isoform of hemoxygenase (HO-2).

the upregulation of the constitutive form of HO-2 in the spinal cord after chronic spinal nerve lesion is most pronounced in the gray matter of the ipsilateral spinal cord and that this upregulation of CO production is most likely contributing to neurodegeneration in the spinal cord.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of CO in the pathophysiology of neuropathic spinal cord damage.
the neurotoxic effects of CO in the spinal cord of the neuropathic rat model.
the role of the constitutive form of heme oxygen-ase-2 (cHO-2) and its metabolite carbon monoxide (cCO) in the development of neuropathic spinal cord pain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
spinal nerve lesion induces up regulation of the constitutive form of the enzyme heme oxygenase-2 in the spinal cord of rats.
the spinal nerve lesion induced upregulation of the constitutive form of HO-2 is associated with the neurodegeneratve changes in the spinal cords of neuropathic rats.
the spinal nerve lesion induced neurodegeneration in the spinal cord is mediated by the upregulated HO-2 expression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
spinal nerve lesion induces a significant upregulation of the constitutive form of HO-2 in the spinal cord of rats, which is associated with the development of neurodegenerative structural changes.
CO is an endogenous neurotoxin in the spinal cord and that its synthesis is upregulated after a chronic nerve lesion, possibly as a response to the nerve damage.
the upregulation of CO production in the spinal cord after spinal nerve lesion may be a contributing factor to spinal cord neurodegenerative events.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spinal cord neurodegenerative process is not limited only to the dorsal horn, but it is a more widespread phenomenon.
the CO produced in response to spinal nerve lesion may be contributing to neurodegeneration.
the CO generated in response to chronic spinal nerve lesion is not beneficial for the survival of neurons and other cells in the spinal cord.
